content:
Following a week of conservative outrage about the release of “Grant Theft Auto VI,” Fox News’ weekend crew couldn’t help but get in on the action.

During Saturday’s edition of the network’s “The Big Weekend Show,” host Joey Jones aimed his outrage not at the perceived “wokeness” of the game or the violence depicted in it ― instead, Jones chose to argue he didn’t like the game simply because he saw it as a waste of time and claimed it could be the reason the U.S. keeps “losing wars.”

The host seemed particularly perturbed after co-host Tomi Lahren told him that many people took the day off work to play the game.

“I think that golf and video games were designed to emasculate men and stop us from doing things like building things and fixing things and creating things,” Jones said.

Jones then lamented the fact that his own network was covering the game’s massive popularity.

“But it’s like, you know what is ‘Grand Theft Auto’ known for? It’s known for debauchery. That’s what made it popular to begin with, is that you can go in there and do terrible things and not get in trouble for it,” Jones said. “And like just that psychological effect on young Americans, maybe that’s why we keep losing wars. I don’t know, but it’s definitely having a detrimental effect.”

Jones is just the latest right-wing voice to disavow the video game, which to date has pulled in record-setting $3.79 billion in sales on its first day.

These criticisms can seemingly be divided into two camps: the old guard of traditional conservatives bemoaning the violence and sexual content present in the game.

The new far right is also complaining about the game being too “woke” and whining about the romantic aspect of it between the game’s two main protagonists.
